correctness.rationale: Define the graph on all 2- and 3-subsets of a fixed 5-set, with inclusion edges, and the ordinary independence flag complex. A deletion-link induction proves any nonzero reduced 5-class needs at least 12 vertices; equality forces an induced six-edge matching. The standalone enumerator exhausts all matchings through size seven and obtains precisely five size-six matchings, each of form M_i. Each yields a signed closed 64-facet integral S5 cycle. On 1320 degree-five simplicial generators, boundaries in degrees 5,6,7 have independent lower-rank checks mod101 of 932,383,97. An explicit 388-by-388 submatrix of [d6|z0..z4] has exact determinant -1, obtained by 388 nonzero unit integer pivots. Boundary-square zero gives the complementary upper bounds rank(d5)<=932 and rank(d6)<=383, so the 388-rank primitive augmented lattice equals the primitive kernel(d5). Hence the five H5 classes are an integral basis. Direct signed-chain checks of every S5 by complement transform show permutation action on basis and negative complement action. Full automorphism group follows from recovering J(5,2) on each bipartite side.

value.rationale: The Desargues/bipartite Kneser graph is a standard incidence graph with unusually large symmetry. A known abstract Z^5 homology group need not be generated by a natural symmetry-invariant collection of primitive shortest geometric spheres, and a rational action does not determine the integral module. The theorem answers whether shortest induced octahedral spheres exist and exhaust integral H5, classifies every minimum-support carrier, and identifies the complete integral signed permutation module. The explicit -1 determinant is a structural integrality assertion with reusable geometric representatives, not a routine Betti-number recomputation or arbitrary cutoff.
